title: Keep the trading allowance at £1,000
headline: Keep £1,000 trading allowance. Raises £0.2bn in 2029-30.
description: The tax-free allowance for small trading and side income rises from £1,000 to £3,000 from April 2027. Switch this on to keep it at £1,000.

baselinePolicy.text: The income tax trading allowance is £3,000 from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 15).

source.quote: This measure increases the tax-free trading and miscellaneous income allowance from £1,000 to £3,000.

alreadyIncludes: The income tax trading allowance is £3,000 from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 15).

lines.title: Trading Allowance: Increase the Income Tax Trading Allowance to £3,000 from £1,000 from 6 April 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
